---
title: "surveyframe and Qualtrics"
description: "How surveyframe relates to Qualtrics: what each does, what surveyframe adds for research, and how to use the 2 together."
---

Qualtrics is a commercial survey platform, used under an institutional or paid licence, which hosts the survey and stores the answers on its servers. surveyframe is a free R package (MIT, on CRAN) for the
whole research workflow around a survey: the questionnaire and its analysis
plan, the collection, the checks, the planned analyses and the APA 7 report.

## What surveyframe adds for research

- An analysis plan declared before the data, with hypotheses and decision
  rules, sealed in the questionnaire file.
- A pre-analysis plan to submit to OSF, Zenodo or an ethics committee.
- A hash anyone can check at [surveyframe.org/verify](https://surveyframe.org/verify/),
  and amendments recorded with their reasons.
- Quality checks, scale reliability, the planned analyses and a report in
  APA 7, in SurveyStudio or in R.

## Using Qualtrics with surveyframe

You can collect with Qualtrics and analyse with surveyframe. Describe the
questionnaire as a surveyframe instrument, with item ids that match the
columns of the exported answers, then read the export:

```r
responses <- read_responses("answers.csv", instrument, respondent_id = "id")
results <- run_analysis_plan(responses, instrument)
```

The plan, the checks and the report then work as they do for answers
surveyframe collected itself.
